events.type: price move: sector selloff plus reversal of a vaccine-stock headline trade
events.summary: Moderna fell 7.75% to $187.46 (from $203.21). It opened at $202.09, touched $212.22 (a new 52-week high, briefly above the roughly $210.58 conversion price of its September bonds), then closed 11.67% below that high (data/prices/MRNA.csv; our calculation). Same day the biotech fund XBI fell 3.39% to $150.90 on 17.2 million shares, 1.93 times its 20-day average volume, while the S&P 500 closed at a record (+0.58%). CNBC called it 'a rough day for many high-flying biotech and healthcare stocks': Grail -10.9%, Novavax -9.9%, Moderna -7.75%. Vaccine stocks also gave back Monday's gains from a plague scare after the WHO said the public risk was low (see next event).
events.why_it_matters: It fired Santi's 5% 'explain big moves' rule. No Moderna news, filing or analyst action caused it; the fall undid Monday's headline-driven jump (from Friday's $190.01 close, Monday plus Tuesday net -1.34%, our calculation). It shows how much of the price is sentiment ahead of the 10-24 data rather than new facts.

events.summary: At a Geneva briefing, WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said a woman who worked at a laboratory in Irkutsk (Siberia) had died and the authorities were checking whether pneumonic plague caused it. WHO estimated the risk 'moderate to low for Irkutsk, a low risk for the Russian Federation as a whole and very low for the WHO European region'; 'no pathogens of dangerous infectious diseases were detected among any of the contacts', and none had symptoms. Cause of death not confirmed; tests under way. Yahoo Finance reported that Novavax fell nearly 10%, giving back a 20% Monday jump 'fueled by concerns about a potential outbreak', and that Moderna 'fell 7%, giving back all its gains from Monday'. Citi said the moves showed 'headline sensitivity' in vaccine companies, which 'remain exposed to volatile policy narratives'.
events.why_it_matters: It is the most specific published reason for the Monday-up, Tuesday-down whipsaw in vaccine stocks. No source says Moderna sells a plague vaccine; plague is a bacterium, and a 24/7 Wall St piece noted Novavax has no plague vaccine either. So this was headline trading, not a change in Moderna's business. Timing caveat: at 9:56 a.m. ET Tuesday Moderna was still +2% at $207.95 with an earlier WHO 'risk appears low' comment already public; the slide came later, alongside the sector-wide drop. The plague reversal and the biotech selloff cannot be cleanly separated.

products.name: intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940), with Merck
products.what_it_is: A personalised mRNA cancer vaccine, made for each patient from the genetic code of their own tumour and given with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda.
products.analogy: Like a 'wanted poster' printed for one patient's own cancer, so their immune system knows exactly which cells to attack.
products.buyers: Hospitals and cancer centres treating patients after melanoma surgery (the Phase 3 is in the adjuvant setting: after surgery, to stop the cancer coming back); paid for by insurers and health systems (inference).
products.how_it_works: The tumour is sequenced and its mutations are identified. Moderna writes an mRNA that codes for up to dozens of those mutation fragments. Injected, it trains T-cells to recognise them, while Keytruda takes the brakes off the immune system.
products.sales: none: not approved. Proxy (analyst opinion): Citi argues the share price already assumes about $13bn a year of cancer-vaccine sales [CNBC, 2026-09-30].
products.stage: Phase 3 (INTerpath-001) met its main goals (relapse-free and distant-metastasis-free survival) per the 2026-08-19 topline; full data at ESMO on 2026-10-24; filing timing not announced. Moderna said nine Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials are under way.
products.size_for_company: Citi's implied $13bn a year would be about 6.7 times Moderna's 2025 revenue of $1.944bn (SEC filings; our calculation). Costs and profits are shared 50/50 with Merck.
products.why_investors_care: It is the main reason for the stock's 535.67% gain this year (data/metrics); the price swings on any sentiment about it.
products.watch_next: ESMO 2026-10-24: size of the benefit, side effects, independent experts' reaction; then filing plans (Q3 call).
